guidance: A continuous-time linear model of a type-II charge-pump loop: it reads the loop bandwidth, phase margin and filter zero and pole for the values entered. Phase-detector sampling, divider delay, VCO input capacitance, charge-pump mismatch and spurs are not modelled, so confirm a marginal design on the bench.
method: A type-II charge-pump PLL is analysed through its continuous-time open-loop gain G(s) = Kphi * Kvco * Z(s) / (N * s), with Kphi = Icp / (2*pi) the phase-detector gain in A/rad, Kvco the VCO gain in rad/s/V and N the feedback divider ratio. The passive loop filter is R2 in series with C1, with C2 from the loop node to ground, so Z(s) = (1 + s*R2*C1) / (s*(C1+C2)*(1 + s*R2*C1*C2/(C1+C2))). It contributes a zero at fz = 1/(2*pi*R2*C1) and a pole at fp = (C1+C2)/(2*pi*R2*C1*C2). Writing K = Kphi*Kvco/(N*(C1+C2)) gives the double-integrator form G(s) = K*(1 + s/(2*pi*fz)) / (s^2*(1 + s/(2*pi*fp))). The page solves |G(j*2*pi*fc)| = 1 for the unity-gain loop bandwidth fc by bisection on log frequency, then reports the phase margin phi = atan(fc/fz) - atan(fc/fp), the filter zero and pole, the natural frequency fn = sqrt(K)/(2*pi) and the second-order damping estimate zeta = sqrt(K)/(2*2*pi*fz), which neglects the filter pole. Inputs are the charge-pump current in microamperes, the VCO gain in MHz/V, the feedback divider ratio, the phase-detector frequency in MHz, R2 in kilohms and C1 and C2 in nanofarads; every field is range-checked with a user-facing message. The loop bandwidth is also expressed as a percentage of the phase-detector frequency, because the continuous-time linear model only holds while fc stays well below that rate. Phase-detector sampling, divider delay, VCO input capacitance, charge-pump mismatch and the reference and supply spurs are not modelled, and the page says so.
